abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is quickly integrated into youth’s daily lives, including their navigation and management of social relationships. The study focuses on college emerging adults’ social use of GenAI, defined as using AI for social purposes. Informed by the Multidimensional Model of Social Media Use, we distinguish between the social enhancement and compensation motives. Survey data from 497 college emerging adults (Mage = 21.58, SD = 2.97) revealed that the social enhancement motive had a more dynamic relationship with socioemotional well-being, associated with higher social competence but also stronger AI attachment; the social compensation motive was related to poorer well-being, associated with lower social competence, greater loneliness, and stronger AI attachment. Dysregulated engagement was the most salient mechanism, followed by intimate self-disclosure to AI. Critical evaluation and contextualised application of AI did not mediate the paths between the motives and well-being. The dual-motive model provides a useful framework to examine AI’s roles in youth’s social development, and identifies dysregulated engagement and intimate self-disclosure as viable targets for intervention.

ur.tldr: 对497名大学新兴成人开展问卷调查，区分生成式AI的社交增强与社交补偿动机。增强动机关联更高社交能力，却伴随更强AI依赖；补偿动机关联孤独、较低幸福感及AI依赖。失调性参与和向AI亲密披露是主要作用机制。

title: Social use of generative artificial intelligence and college emerging adults’ socioemotional well-being: a dual-motive approach
title_zh: 生成式人工智能的社会性使用与大学新兴成年人的社会情绪福祉：双动机方法
